title: Expose Gmsh 3D meshing controls for conformal and standalone exports
body:
## Summary

Expose independent Gmsh volume-meshing controls on all three volume-export paths:

- `export_dagmc_h5m_file(unstructured_volumes=..., ...)` for a combined conformal DAGMC surface and tetrahedral tally mesh.
- `export_unstructured_mesh_file(...)` for standalone VTK volume meshes.
- `export_gmsh_mesh_file(dimensions=3, ...)` for native 3D Gmsh meshes.

### User API

- `mesh_algorithm_3d=1` sets `Mesh.Algorithm3D` independently of the existing 2D `mesh_algorithm`. The default remains Delaunay; `10` selects HXT.
- `volume_mesh_options=None` accepts a dictionary of numeric or string Gmsh options. A non-empty dictionary is applied **after surface meshing and immediately before volume meshing**, allowing volume-only sizing and optimization overrides.
- Dictionary entries take precedence over the corresponding named settings for the volume step. Surface-only exports ignore the dictionary; non-Gmsh backends warn when these controls are supplied.

The [README](https://github.com/fusion-energy/cad_to_dagmc/blob/gmsh-volume-mesh-options/README.md#gmsh-3d-meshing-controls) now has complete executable examples for **both combined conformal export and standalone 3D export**, plus defaults, precedence and limitations. Backend and output documentation is updated as well.

### Conformality and compatibility

The combined export reuses the surface triangulation already written to H5M when generating tetrahedra for the selected volumes. Separate export calls do not share mesh state.

Existing positional arguments remain usable. With no volume options or an empty dictionary, direct exports retain a single `generate(3)` call, and combined exports retain their existing `generate(2)` then `generate(3)` sequence. Options are isolated to each export session, including error cleanup.

Relaxed interior sizing does not guarantee zero refinement or a speedup. Options that change element order, recombine elements or force remeshing can invalidate the first-order conformal DAGMC/tally pairing.

## Validation

- **185 passed, 3 skipped** across the affected export, sizing, volume-selection, backend-selection and Gmsh cleanup regression tests using the h5py backend.
- Includes **54 new tests**, with **12 written-file conformity cases** comparing H5M triangles against actual VTK tetrahedron boundary faces. Covers Delaunay/HXT, default/relaxed interior sizing, curved geometry, touching volumes and selected-volume export, including the shared internal interface.

title: Add imprint_glue and remove the cadquery direct-mesh plugin backend
body:
## imprint_glue

`export_dagmc_h5m_file`, `export_unstructured_mesh_file` and `export_gmsh_mesh_file` take a new `imprint_glue` argument. It's keyword-only on the latter two, since they already have `*`. The value is passed to cadquery's `imprint(..., glue=...)` (CadQuery/cadquery#2069), either directly for the gmsh backend or through cad-to-dagmc-mesher's own imprint.

| `imprint_glue` | |
|---|---|
| `"partial"` (default) | Fastest, lowest RAM. For solids that touch or share faces, fully or in part, without faces crossing or solids overlapping |
| `"full"` | Only for shared faces that coincide exactly. Faces that only partly coincide are not split. Despite the name it is the least thorough |
| `None` | Glue off: full general-fuse intersection. Slowest, most thorough |

`imprint` is unchanged: on/off, or an int thread count. The two combine, e.g. `imprint=4, imprint_glue=None`. Invalid values are rejected before any imprinting happens. Documented in `docs/advanced/imprinting.md`.

## Removing the cadquery backend

The direct-mesh plugin imprints inside `toMesh` with no way to pass a glue option, and the package has fallen behind. So `meshing_backend="cadquery"`, the `cadquery_direct_mesh_plugin` dependency and `share_coincident_face_ids` (only needed for the plugin) are removed.
- `meshing_backend="cadquery"` now raises a `ValueError` that points to `"cad-to-dagmc-mesher"` (same `tolerance`/`angular_tolerance` arguments) or `"gmsh"`.
- `tolerance`/`angular_tolerance` now select the mesher outright, so there's no more "accepted by both" warning. Combined with gmsh-only arguments they still raise the ambiguity error.
- With no backend arguments and no mesher installed (e.g. a conda install), it falls back to gmsh with a warning instead of to cadquery. With mesher arguments and no mesher installed, it raises `CadToDagmcMesherNotFoundError` naming the arguments that selected it.

title: Keep shared faces shared when scaling, and document meshing pre-imprinted BREP files
body:
## Bug
Users who need more control over imprinting can imprint the geometry themselves, save a BREP, load it and export with `imprint=False`. This works unless the geometry is scaled. `add_cadquery_object(scale_factor=...)` and the cad-to-dagmc-mesher backend's export `scale_factor` both scaled each solid on its own. That transforms a face two solids share once per solid, so each solid ended up with its own copy, and the h5m got two coincident one-sided surfaces instead of one surface with a sense for each volume. Nothing reported it.

Fix: new `_scale_together` scales the solids as one compound, so each shared face is transformed once. The output keeps the input order and count, and it's used in both places. gmsh export-time scaling already worked because gmsh scales after importing the whole model.

Measured with a small box on part of a big box's face, imprinted, saved as BREP and exported with `imprint=False`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| mesher, export `scale_factor=10` | 0 shared surfaces | 1 |
| mesher / gmsh, `add_cadquery_object(scale_factor=10)` | 0 | 1 |
| gmsh, export `scale_factor=10` | 1 | 1 |

`tests/test_scale_shared_faces.py` covers the helper, `add_cadquery_object`, and h5m files written by both backends with scaling at either point. The h5m tests need pydagmc and are skipped without it. Four of these tests fail on main and all pass with this fix.

## Docs
New section in `docs/advanced/imprinting.md`, "Meshing Geometry You Imprinted Yourself". It's a runnable example: imprint with CadQuery, `exportBrep`, `importBrep`, then `imprint=False` with the mesher and `scale_factor=10`. It also warns that STEP files don't keep the shared faces, so the shared face comes back as two coincident copies. There's a link to it from the advanced options index.

title: Scale STEP assemblies after placing their parts
body:
## Problem

`add_stp_file(..., material_tags="assembly_names" | "assembly_materials", scale_factor=...)` rebuilt the imported assembly by scaling each top-level child's shape and re-adding it at its **unscaled** `loc`. Two consequences:

- **Silently wrong geometry.** A part placed by an assembly location (the normal case in STEP files from real CAD tools) stays at its unscaled position. A 10 mm box at x = 100 mm scaled by 0.1 ended up at x = 99.5–100.5 cm instead of 9.5–10.5 cm, while the same file loaded with a list of tags was correct.
- **Crash on nested assemblies.** A sub-assembly child has `obj is None`, so `child.obj.scale(...)` raised `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'scale'`.

The existing `test_stp_file_with_assembly_names_and_scale_factor` didn't catch this because it places its parts inside the shapes (`moveTo`), not with assembly locations, and it only checks the tags.

## Fix

Pass `scale_factor` through to `add_cadquery_object`, which already handles it correctly: it flattens the assembly with `toCompound()` (locations applied), then scales all solids together with `_scale_together`. Tag extraction is unchanged, and materials are now kept for `assembly_materials` because the assembly is no longer rebuilt.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_stp_file_with_assembly_tags.py`:
- `test_stp_file_with_assembly_names_scales_part_locations`: a part placed by `loc` lands at the scaled position, matching the list-of-tags path.
- `test_stp_file_with_nested_assembly_names_and_scale_factor`: a nested sub-assembly loads, keeps its tags in order, and every part's bounds are 0.1× the unscaled bounds.

Both fail on `main` (one with the wrong position, one with the `AttributeError`) and pass with the fix. Locally, the full suite (`tests/`, without the transport tests, which need OpenMC in the same environment) gave 529 passed, 24 skipped, and `ruff check .` is clean.

title: Auto-refine makes the mesh depend on free RAM: same inputs give different meshes, and particle losses, on a busy machine
body:
## What happens

The same `export_dagmc_h5m_file` call on the same STEP file, with the same arguments, produced two different meshes and different transport results. The only difference was how busy the machine was.

`cad_to_dagmc` calls cad-to-dagmc-mesher's `mesh_assembly` with `auto_refine` on (the mesher's default) and without `memory_budget_gb`. The mesher then sizes its refinement budget from the machine's state at that moment (`_memory_ceiling_bytes` in `cad_to_dagmc_mesher/cad/_assembly.py`):

```python
available = _available_memory_bytes()
current = _current_rss_bytes() or _peak_rss_bytes() or 0
return _REFINE_MEMORY_FRACTION * (current + available)   # 0.75
```

When a projected refinement round would exceed that budget, refinement stops and the unrefined mesh is written with only a printed warning. So the mesh depends on how much memory other processes happen to be using.

## Measured

A 64-solid stellarator model (radial build, 44 winding packs, building), tolerance 0.5 cm, angular tolerance 0.2, imprinted on 1 thread. cad_to_dagmc main (c611da2) with cad-to-dagmc-mesher 0.3.7. Same command both times:

| | Machine busy (other jobs running) | Machine idle |
|---|---|---|
| Refinement budget | 12.3 GB | about 37 GB (75% of 4.2 GB RSS + 45.0 GB free) |
| What auto-refine did | stopped before round 1: "projected to need 12.4GB, above the 12.3GB budget (38 solid(s) still fold)" | refined the folding winding packs to 0.25 cm and finished |
| Triangles | 1,455,738 | 1,543,488 |
| Lost particles in OpenMC, 1e6 histories | **25,994 (2.6%)**, all in the winding packs | **0** |
| Winding-pack flux | 40.17 | 40.68 (+1.3%) |

Both runs exit 0 and write `reactor-dagmc.h5m`. Nothing in the file records that refinement was cut short. The only sign is a log line that's easy to miss in a long log.

## Why it matters

- **Reproducibility:** the same inputs and versions give a different h5m, and different answers, depending on what else is running: CI runners, shared workstations, parallel batch jobs.
- **Silent degradation:** under memory pressure, the result is a known-folding mesh that loses particles, rather than an error.
- **No control from cad_to_dagmc:** `export_dagmc_h5m_file` exposes neither `auto_refine` nor `memory_budget_gb`, so a user can't pin the behaviour.

## Suggestions

1. **Make the default deterministic.** For example, use a fixed default budget, or none, rather than one derived from available RAM, so a given input always gives the same mesh. If memory then runs out, that's a loud failure rather than a quietly different mesh.
2. **Fail rather than degrade.** If refinement can't finish within the budget, either raise an error (with a flag to accept a partial result) or at least emit a `UserWarning` from cad_to_dagmc, not only a print.
3. **Expose the settings** in `export_dagmc_h5m_file`: `auto_refine` and `memory_budget_gb` (and perhaps `max_refine_rounds`).
4. **Record the outcome in the h5m**: final per-solid tolerances, and whether refinement finished. Then a mesh can be checked later against the conditions it was made under.

title: Keep cad-to-dagmc-mesher's refinement report (#240)
body:
The cad_to_dagmc side of #240, trimmed to add **no user settings**. The mesher side, fusion-energy/cad-to-dagmc-mesher#208 (merged), already makes the default deterministic: the same inputs give the same mesh whatever the free memory, or a `RefinementMemoryError`. So cad_to_dagmc doesn't need settings for it.

## What this changes

- **`self.refinement`** keeps cad-to-dagmc-mesher's auto-refine report from the last `export_dagmc_h5m_file`: rounds, convergence, remaining folds, final per-solid tolerances, and per-round memory. It's `None` when no refinement ran, and it's reset at each export so a stale report can't outlive its export. Before, the report was dropped and the only record was printed output.

```python
model.export_dagmc_h5m_file(meshing_backend="cad-to-dagmc-mesher", tolerance=0.5)
model.refinement["converged"], model.refinement["remaining_folds"]
```

An earlier version of this PR added `auto_refine`, `memory_budget_gb` and `max_refine_rounds`. They're removed again, and a test now asserts they're rejected as unknown keyword arguments.

`tests/test_refinement_report.py`:

- a later export without refinement clears it;
- the three refinement options are rejected.

title: Require cad-to-dagmc-mesher 0.4.1 or newer
body:
Raises the minimum cad-to-dagmc-mesher version from 0.3.7 to 0.4.1.

0.4.0 makes auto-refine give the same mesh regardless of how much memory is free (fixes #240): memory can change how long refinement takes, never the mesh it produces, and if the mesh cannot fit it raises `RefinementMemoryError` rather than returning a coarser one. It also meshes each face at its own tolerance with watertight shared edges, and keeps unchanged faces between refinement rounds, so refinement is faster and the meshes are usually smaller.

0.4.1 stops auto-refine refining for zero-thickness (flat) folds, which no tolerance can fix. With 0.4.0 the model zoo SimpleTokamak test at tolerance 0.01 refined for them, needed more memory than some CI runners have free, and raised `RefinementMemoryError` (fusion-energy/cad-to-dagmc-mesher#213).

- With `scale_factor=100` the old 0.01 is a 0.1 mm deflection, which the docs already warned can produce an enormous mesh and exhaust memory, and they recommended 0.5 instead.

The chordal tolerance is in cm after `scale_factor`, which should bring the CAD to cm for OpenMC, so the default is a 5 mm deflection. The gmsh backend is unchanged.

title: Imprint with cadquery's Assembly.imprint
body:
Draft that uses CadQuery/cadquery#2128 (`Assembly.imprint`) and shows what the new method lets cad_to_dagmc remove. It keeps working with stable CadQuery (2.8.0) through a fallback marked for removal, so it no longer has to wait for a CadQuery release, only for CadQuery/cadquery#2128 to be merged.

## What changes

`Assembly.imprint` imprints each part of the assembly in place. The imprinted solids therefore stay in the order the parts were added, and the material tags stay on their own volumes without any remapping. That removes:

- `get_ids_from_assembly`, `get_ids_from_imprinted_assembly` and `order_material_ids_by_brep_order`, which mapped imprinted solids back to their origins and reordered the tags to match
- the tests for them, including all of `test_loading_from_file_vs_shape_object.py` and `test_cadquery_compatibility.py`

`imprint_assembly` now returns the imprinted compound, one solid per part in part order. It raises a clear "Overlapping solids" error if imprinting splits a part into several solids. Before, the gmsh paths gave a count mismatch between volumes and material tags. With the default glue, the gmsh paths now refuse the same overlaps as the mesher (coincident-face overlaps and swallowed solids), and `docs/advanced/overlaps.md` says so.

## Stable CadQuery fallback (temporary)

CadQuery 2.8.0 has no `Assembly.imprint`. When it is missing, `imprint_assembly` uses the functional imprint, puts the imprinted solids back in part order from its origins map, and raises the same overlap error. The rest of the code sees the same result either way. On the legacy signature, `"full"` and `None` glue raise `RuntimeError` as on main. `pyproject.toml` stays at `cadquery>=2.8.0`. Every piece of the fallback has a TODO to remove it once CadQuery/cadquery#2128 is released and required:

- `_imprint_assembly_without_assembly_imprint` and the `hasattr` check in `src/cad_to_dagmc/core.py`
- `HAS_ASSEMBLY_IMPRINT` / `HAS_GLUE` branches in `tests/test_imprint_threads.py` and `tests/test_imprint_glue.py`, and the legacy-signature tests
- the `functional` param of the `imprint_implementation` fixture in `tests/test_imprint_assembly.py`, which runs the order, shared face, separate part, overlap and gmsh h5m tag tests against both implementations
- the `assembly-imprint` CI matrix entry and the `pyproject.toml` comment

title: cad-to-dagmc-mesher spends most of its export time in the pre-imprint CAD overlap check on tokamak models
body:
On paramak tokamak models most of the cad-to-dagmc-mesher export time is spent in the CAD overlap check that runs before imprinting, not in meshing. With that check skipped the mesher is as fast as or faster than gmsh on every model I tried, while still producing geometry that transports without lost particles. With the check, it is slower than gmsh on most of them.

## Numbers

Time is the wall time of `export_dagmc_h5m_file` only (the CAD build is not included). Each h5m was then transported in OpenMC with 10 batches of 10,000 particles from a 14 MeV point source at the centre of the geometry, with lost-particle aborts turned off so every lost particle is counted (counted as `No intersection found with DAGMC cell` warnings). Everything ran one case at a time on the same machine.

| model (paramak, 180 degrees) | gmsh, min/max mesh size 5/50 | gmsh, 1/20 | mesher, defaults | mesher, CAD overlap check skipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sparc_from_2020_paper` | 10.2 s, 9k tris, 0 lost | 24.5 s, 37k, 0 | 92.9 s, 44k, 0 | **10.2 s**, 44k, 0 |
| `iter_from_2020_paper` | 55.9 s, 43k, 0 | 483 s, 265k, 0 | 87.9 s, 92k, 0 | **29.2 s**, 92k, 0 |
| `eu_demo_from_2015_paper` | 67.8 s, 85k, 0 | 581 s, 515k, 0 | 115 s, 181k, 0 | **46.2 s**, 181k, 0 |
| ARC (`arc_from_2026_paper`, in paramak PR 457) | 27.9 s, 48k, **1195 lost** | 140 s, 258k, 0 | 78.4 s, 91k, 0 | **19.9 s**, 91k, 0 |
| `tokamak_from_plasma` | 27.3 s, 18k, 0 | 224 s, 106k, 0 | 19.5 s, 72k, 0 | **11.7 s**, 72k, 0 |
| `tokamak_from_plasma` with toroidal sectors | 20.0 s, 12k, 0 | 126 s, 67k, 0 | 88.8 s, 39k, 0 | **20.3 s**, 39k, 0 |
| `spherical_tokamak` with PF coils | 14.1 s, 13k, 0 | 91.5 s, 68k, 0 | 37.1 s, 85k, 0 | **16.6 s**, 85k, 0 |

Skipping the check gives exactly the same triangle counts as the default run, so it does not change the mesh, it only costs time. ARC is the interesting case: it has a 0.5 cm tungsten first wall, gmsh at 5/50 loses particles there and needs 1/20 (140 s) to be transportable, while the mesher gets it right at its defaults and, without the overlap check, in 20 s.

## Where the time goes

The check is `_raise_for_cad_overlaps` / `_find_cad_overlaps` in `cad_to_dagmc_mesher/cad/_assembly.py`. It runs an OCC common (boolean) on every pair of solids whose bounding boxes overlap, one pair after another, until `_OVERLAP_TIME_BUDGET_S = 60` runs out.

Tokamak models are close to the worst case for this:

- The parts are nested shells (plasma inside the vessel inside the blanket, coils around everything), so bounding box culling removes very few pairs.
- The pairs are revolved spline surfaces that touch or nearly touch, which is where OCC does the full calculation even though they share no volume (the comment above `_OVERLAP_TIME_BUDGET_S` describes this).

On SPARC (39 solids) the warning below was printed 86 s into the export, and the imprint and meshing that followed took about 11 s:

```
WARNING: CAD overlap check ran out of its 60s budget with 89 solid pair(s) unchecked, so overlapping input may not have been caught here. Imprint's own origins still cover every solid, as does the mesh-level overlap check after meshing.
```

So for these models the check usually spends a minute or more and still does not finish, and as the warning says, the overlap checks that run later already cover every solid. The mesh-level check (`find_solid_overlaps`) took 0.45 s on the same SPARC model.

## Possible improvements

Any one of these would make the mesher the faster choice for paramak models:

1. **Allow the check to be skipped or its budget set** from `export_dagmc_h5m_file`, for example `check_cad_overlaps=False` or a time budget argument. Callers that already check for overlaps themselves (paramak's tests imprint every reactor and fail on any solid with two origins) could turn it off.
2. **Run the pairwise booleans in parallel.** The loop is single threaded while imprint and meshing use every core (32 threads here).
3. **Cheaper test before the boolean.** For example, a `BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape` distance above zero proves a pair shares no volume without a full common.
4. **Rely on the later checks** (imprint origins and the mesh-level overlap check) when the pre-imprint check would not finish within its budget anyway.

## Reproduce

```python
# pip install paramak==0.11.0 cad_to_dagmc
import time
import paramak
from cad_to_dagmc import CadToDagmc

reactor = paramak.sparc_from_2020_paper(rotation_angle=180)
tags = [f"mat_{i}" for i, (obj, *_) in enumerate(reactor) for _ in obj.Solids()]

model = CadToDagmc()
model.add_cadquery_object(cadquery_object=reactor, material_tags=tags)
start = time.perf_counter()
model.export_dagmc_h5m_file(filename="dagmc.h5m", meshing_backend="cad-to-dagmc-mesher")
print(f"{time.perf_counter() - start:.1f} s")

# for comparison, skip the pre-imprint CAD overlap check
import cad_to_dagmc_mesher.cad._assembly as mesher_assembly
mesher_assembly._OVERLAP_TIME_BUDGET_S = 0.0
start = time.perf_counter()
model.export_dagmc_h5m_file(filename="dagmc_no_check.h5m", meshing_backend="cad-to-dagmc-mesher")
print(f"{time.perf_counter() - start:.1f} s")
```

## Environment

- cad_to_dagmc 0.16.0, cad-to-dagmc-mesher 0.5.0, gmsh 4.15.2
- cadquery 2.8.0, cadquery-ocp 7.9.3.1.1
- openmc 0.16.1.dev0
- Python 3.12, Linux, 32 threads

title: Pass the mesher's overlap message on, in the caller's material tags
body:
## What was wrong

When cad-to-dagmc-mesher found overlapping solids, `_mesh_with_cad_to_dagmc_mesher` re-raised it as a fixed message that named only the material tags involved:

```
Overlapping solids in the CAD. The solids tagged ['steel', 'water'] could not be told apart after imprinting. ...
```

That dropped everything the mesher reported: which pairs overlap, by how much and where. "Could not be told apart after imprinting" is also wrong for the common case, which the mesher catches before imprinting.

## What this changes

The mesher's message is passed on whole. Its per-solid names (`steel#0`) are turned back into the caller's tags, with the input position at first mention (`'steel' (solid 0)`). With fusion-energy/cad-to-dagmc-mesher#234, a slab pushed 0.01 cm into the block it sits on gives:

```
Overlapping solids in the CAD:
  'steel' (solid 0) and 'water' (solid 1) overlap by 100 cm³ along a contact surface (0.020% of 'steel', 0.1% of 'water'): a layer about 0.01 cm thick, spanning 100 x 100 x 0.01 cm around (0, 0, -0.005)
DAGMC requires every point to belong to exactly one volume, ... Boolean-subtract the overlap in CAD (e.g. b = b.cut(a)) so every point belongs to exactly one solid. An overlap along a contact surface is two faces meant to touch, one modelled slightly into the other; moving that face back to the contact works as well as the cut. To mesh the rest of the model meanwhile, leave one solid of each pair out.
```

With the current mesher release the same pair already reads `'steel' (solid 0) and 'water' (solid 1) share 100 mm^3 (...)`, which is more than the tags alone.

## Tests

In `tests/test_overlapping_solids.py`:

- **The two wordings:** a sphere sunk in a box, and a face pressed into its neighbour. These tests skip when the installed mesher does not describe the overlap. That skip is temporary: a TODO says to raise the mesher pin to the first release with fusion-energy/cad-to-dagmc-mesher#234 and remove it.
- **Name translation:** the mesher's message reaches the user whole, in the caller's tags. This runs against a stand-in `mesh_assembly`, so it does not depend on the mesher version.

Locally, the file passes with the mesher branch (8 passed), and with mesher 0.5.0 (6 passed, 2 skipped).

title: Add CadToDagmc.check_overlaps, and document checking CAD for overlaps
Cut repetition from the docs and fix what they got wrong
body:
The same examples and rules were repeated across pages, and the copies had drifted apart. The `set_size` example with coarse, fine and global boxes was on six pages, OpenMC setup code on eight, and the backend selection rules on three, with different details in each. Each topic is now explained once, on the page you would look for it, and the other pages link to it:

- how the meshing backend is chosen: `meshing/index.md`, new section "How the Backend Is Chosen"
- `scale_factor` and the units of mesh sizes: `advanced/geometry_scaling.md`
- imprint glue modes and when to turn imprinting off: `advanced/imprinting.md`
- overlaps: `advanced/overlaps.md`

Meshing now comes before Outputs in the sidebar, because every output page depends on the meshing arguments. The docs are about 1,500 lines shorter.

I checked the claims against the code (cad_to_dagmc, cad-to-dagmc-mesher 0.7.0, CadQuery 2.8.0, DAGMC) and ran them where that was quicker. These were wrong:

- Tag length. The h5m writer stores `mat:` plus the tag in a 32-byte name that needs a null byte at the end, so tags must be 27 characters or fewer, not 28. With 28-character tags OpenMC 0.15.3 fails to find the materials, and with 27 it loads. The implicit complement tag also carries `_comp`, so its limit is 22.
- Reserved names. `void` and `graveyard` are reserved as well as `vacuum`, in any case. A volume tagged `vacuum` is void, so particles cross it. They are not lost.
- The mm to m scale factor is 0.001, not 0.01.
- The OpenMC examples used the DAGMC universe as the root universe. cad_to_dagmc writes no graveyard, so they now use `bounded_universe()`.
- Gmsh physical groups are paired with volumes by position, and which volumes a group holds is never checked. A `.msh` file with physical groups needs `Mesh.SaveAll`, or it has no surface triangles. assembly-mesh-plugin adds a `mat:<material>` group for each part that has a `cq.Material`, which breaks the count, and it does not imprint.
- CadQuery's STEP reader treats a part whose name ends in `_part` as the shape of its parent, so `"assembly_names"` and `"assembly_materials"` leave it out without an error. The STEP example used names like that.
- The overlap checks an export runs need the cad-to-dagmc-mesher backend and imprinting. The Gmsh backend writes overlapping solids without an error.
- The CadQuery > 2.6.1 notes are gone, since cadquery>=2.8.0 is required.
- The algorithm table listed Gmsh's 7, 8 and 9 with no warning. With Gmsh 4.15 they fail on simple solids, and 11 makes quads that cad_to_dagmc reads as triangles.

Several examples that pytest-codeblocks used to skip now run.

`pytest --codeblocks docs/` gives 42 passed, 37 skipped (main: 42 passed, 106 skipped). `sphinx-build docs` gives the same single warning as main, that sphinxcadquery has no `setup()`.

Not changed here, because they are code rather than docs:

- `check_material_tags` warns only above 28 characters, and should warn above 27. The implicit complement tag and the Gmsh conversion functions are not checked at all.
- Some docstrings on the API page are wrong. Two give the mesher's default tolerance as 0.01 (it is 0.5), `add_stp_file` describes `filename` as "the filename used to save the html graph", and `add_cadquery_object` says it returns the number of volumes in the stp file.
- `export_gmsh_file_to_dagmc_h5m_file` leaves its gmsh session open when it raises the tag-count `ValueError`.

title: Warn about tags too long for the h5m file
body:
Follow-up to #252, which found that the tag length check was off by one and missed some tags.

The h5m writers store `mat:` plus the tag in a 32-byte group name, and DAGMC reads it as a null-terminated string. So a material tag can have at most 27 characters, and an implicit complement tag, which also gets `_comp`, at most 22. Before this change:

- `check_material_tags` warned only above 28 characters, so a 28-character tag passed without a warning and OpenMC then failed to find its material.
- The implicit complement tag was not checked at all.
- `export_gmsh_file_to_dagmc_h5m_file` and `export_gmsh_object_to_dagmc_h5m_file` did not check any tag.

Now `_check_tag_lengths` warns about both kinds of tag. It runs when parts are added (as before), on the implicit complement tag in `export_dagmc_h5m_file`, and on all tags in the two Gmsh conversion functions. The limits are worked out from the 32-byte name size, so the reason for them is in the code. These are still warnings, as before, not errors.

The two doc pages that said these checks were missing are updated.

`tests/test_tag_lengths.py` checks 27 vs 28 characters for material tags, 22 vs 23 for the implicit complement tag on export, and both Gmsh conversion functions. Four of its five tests fail on main.

title: Fix wrong API docstrings
body:
Follow-up to #252, which found these wrong docstrings on the API page:

- `export_unstructured_mesh_file` and `export_dagmc_h5m_file` gave the cad-to-dagmc-mesher `tolerance` default as 0.01, a 0.1 mm deflection. The default is `DEFAULT_TOLERANCE = 0.5`, a 5 mm deflection on geometry scaled to cm.
- `add_stp_file` described `filename` as "the filename used to save the html graph". It is now "the path of the STEP file to load".
- `add_cadquery_object` said it returns the number of volumes in the stp file. It returns the number of volumes added from the CadQuery object.

Only docstrings change.

title: Finalize gmsh when export_gmsh_file_to_dagmc_h5m_file raises
body:
Follow-up to #252, which found this bug.

`export_gmsh_file_to_dagmc_h5m_file` opens its own gmsh session. When the number of material tags did not match the number of volumes, it raised a `ValueError` before reaching `gmsh.finalize()`, so the session stayed open. A file gmsh could not open did the same. The opening, the tag count check and the triangle extraction now run in a `try`, and gmsh is finalized in the `finally`, as the other export paths already do (#187).

There is a new test in `tests/test_gmsh_session_cleanup.py`. It passes too few tags for `tests/tagged_mesh.msh` and checks that gmsh is no longer initialized afterwards. It fails on main.

title: Reject a solid that is in two parts as an overlap when it is added
body:
Two parts holding the same solid both claim its region, so that is an overlap whatever the geometry looks like. This rejects it when the geometry is added, with the usual "Overlapping solids in the CAD" error naming the parts.

## Why

Imprinting overlapping parts with CadQuery's `Assembly.imprint` (CadQuery/cadquery#2128, used by #247) leaves the region the parts share in both of them. Exporting that assembly with `imprint=False` skips the overlap checks that come with the export's own imprint. CadQuery's `Solids()` drops the repeated solid, so the user got this instead:

```
ValueError: When setting material_tags the number of material_tags
should be equal to the number of volumes in the CAD
geometry 3 volumes found in model
and 4 material_tags found
```

This came up while working on #247. The check is independent of it, so it can go in separately, and #247 picks it up from `main`.

## What changes

`add_cadquery_object` walks every occurrence of every solid with `TopExp_Explorer` (which, unlike `Solids()`, does not deduplicate) and raises before the material tags are read if any solid is there more than once:

- in two parts of an assembly: `Parts 'a' and 'b' hold the same solid`
- twice in one part: `Part 'a' holds the same solid more than once`
- twice in a plain compound: `The CadQuery object holds the same solid more than once`
- already added by an earlier call: `Part 'a' holds a solid already added to the model by an earlier add_cadquery_object call`. The model keeps the solids it was given before scaling, since scaling makes new solids.

Counting solids per part could not tell this apart from a legitimate part made of several separate solids. A repeated solid can, and is never valid. One shape placed at several locations is several different solids, so reusing a part in an assembly is still fine.

`docs/advanced/overlaps.md` says this check runs on add, whatever the backend or `imprint`.

## Tests

New `tests/test_repeated_solids.py` (18 tests):

- rejected: the same solid in two parts (with `assembly_names`, `assembly_materials` and a tag list), in three parts, several repeated solids reported in one error, twice in one part, twice in a compound, nested parts named by their own name
- the model is left unchanged when an object is rejected, and later calls are still checked
- across calls: the same solid added again (with and without `scale_factor`), and an assembly part repeating an earlier solid, are rejected; the same shape moved is accepted
- still accepted: one shape reused at different locations, a part made of several separate solids
- only on a CadQuery with `Assembly.imprint` (skipped in this repo's CI until `main` tests it, as #247 does): overlapping parts imprinted by the user are rejected, and touching parts imprinted by the user keep their names and order and export with `imprint=False`, with each material on the right volume in the h5m

The 10 rejection tests fail against `main` without this change. The guards pass either way, as they should.

Full suite locally, with the inspector and cad-to-dagmc-mesher 0.7.0 installed: stable CadQuery 2.8.0 **629 passed, 12 skipped**; CadQuery/cadquery#2128 head `27b5290c` **635 passed, 6 skipped**.

## Test dependency

`dagmc-h5m-file-inspector` is added to the `tests` extra. Nothing installed it, so `tests/test_overlapping_solids.py`, which skips at module level without it, never ran in CI. It needs only `h5py` and `numpy`, and with it installed (and cad-to-dagmc-mesher 0.7.0) all of that file passes locally.

## Not covered

The check compares solid objects, not geometry. Separately made solids that happen to be identical, such as one STEP file loaded twice, are not caught; `model.check_overlaps()` finds those.

title: Document meshing an assembly imprinted with Assembly.imprint
body:
Draft. Documents meshing an assembly the user imprinted with CadQuery's `Assembly.imprint` (CadQuery/cadquery#2128), including subassemblies imprinted with different glue. `Assembly.imprint` is not in a CadQuery release yet, so this is ready for when it is.

## What changes

New sections in `docs/advanced/imprinting.md`, under "Meshing Geometry You Imprinted Yourself":

- **Imprinting an Assembly in Memory:** `assembly.imprint()`, then `add_cadquery_object(assembly, material_tags="assembly_names")` and `imprint=False`. Parts keep their names and order through the imprint, so no BREP file is needed. Notes that a one-part assembly cannot be imprinted.
- **Different Glue for Different Subassemblies:** imprint each subassembly with its own glue, add them to one assembly, then imprint that once more to connect them. The last imprint needs the glue the contacts *between* the subassemblies need: `"full"` is enough where those faces coincide exactly, even for a subassembly imprinted with `"partial"` (its faces were already split), and `"partial"` is needed where a contact between subassemblies is only partial.
- A warning that `Assembly.add` stores a copy of a subassembly (`arg._copy()`), so imprinting the original after adding it leaves the combined assembly unimprinted, with no error. Imprint before adding, or imprint the copy through `combined.objects["name"]`.

`docs/advanced/index.md` gets a row pointing to both.

## How the examples are tested

Both examples carry `<!--pytest.mark.skipif(not hasattr(cadquery.Assembly, "imprint"), ...)-->`, so `pytest --codeblocks` skips them on CadQuery without `Assembly.imprint` and runs them, with no change here, once the docs job installs a CadQuery release that has it. A TODO comment marks the "not yet in a CadQuery release" wording to update then.

Checked locally:

| CadQuery | `pytest --codeblocks docs/advanced/imprinting.md` |
|---|---|
| stable 2.8.0 | 2 passed, 3 skipped (the 2 new examples, plus the existing skipped block) |
| CadQuery/cadquery#2128 head `4c49a3a3` | 4 passed, 1 skipped |

On the PR head the h5m files are right: the mixed glue example gives `{1: 'armour', 2: 'structure', 3: 'blanket', 4: 'pipe'}` and 22 DAGMC surfaces for the 22 distinct faces of the imprinted compound, so every shared face is written once.

Behind the docs, with the CadQuery PR head:

| Order | contacts connected |
|---|---|
| imprint subassemblies, `add()`, `combined.imprint(glue="full")` | all |
| `add()`, then imprint the original subassemblies | none |
| ...then `combined.imprint(glue="full")` | all but the partial contact inside a subassembly |
| `add()`, then imprint `combined.objects[...]`, then `combined.imprint(glue="full")` | all |
| partial contact between subassemblies, last imprint `"full"` | not between the subassemblies |
| same, last imprint `"partial"` | all |

## Before merging

- [ ] A CadQuery release includes `Assembly.imprint`
- [ ] Name that release in the docs (see the TODO), and check the examples ran in the docs job
- [x] Mention that overlapping parts imprinted this way are rejected on add (#256, now merged)
